title: House Floor Debate
subtitle: H.R.3050 — American Energy Independence and Production Act

metadata.laymanSummary: The House narrowly passed a bill expanding oil and gas drilling permits, fast-tracking LNG export terminals, and reversing Biden-era energy regulations, with Republicans arguing it cuts energy costs.

data.billTitle: American Energy Independence and Production Act — Expanding federal drilling permits and fast-tracking LNG export infrastructure

speakers.name: Rep. Mike Johnson
speakers.title: R-LA · House Speaker
speakers.quote: American energy independence means Americans are not held hostage by OPEC, by Putin, or by supply chains we don't control. Every barrel of oil we produce here is one less barrel that funds a foreign adversary. This bill lowers gas prices at the pump and strengthens our national security simultaneously.

speakers.name: Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez
speakers.title: D-NY · House Oversight
speakers.quote: The last time we had record domestic oil production, gas was still $3.50 a gallon because oil companies set global prices, not domestic production levels. This bill doesn't lower gas prices — it increases oil company profits. And it will guarantee we miss every climate target we have committed to internationally.

speakers.name: Rep. Kat Cammack
speakers.title: R-FL
speakers.quote: Energy poverty is a real crisis in this country. Florida families are paying $400 a month more for utilities than they were four years ago. Affordable, reliable energy is not optional — it is a fundamental necessity. This bill gets government out of the way and lets American ingenuity produce the energy we need.

data.title: What This Vote Means
data.text: H.R.3050 passed 220-215, with no Democrats voting in favor. It streamlines federal oil and gas drilling permits, requires the Interior Department to hold quarterly offshore lease sales, and waives several environmental review requirements for LNG export terminals under construction. Critics note the EIA projects the bill would increase domestic production by 400,000 barrels/day while having minimal impact on retail gas prices, which are set by global markets.
